design.hintAuthority: Only actual move_target_busy produces an in-memory hint. Hint binds original run/thread, complete lease/token generation and exact current boundary; it is never proof or replay authority. Startup rediscovers durable unresolved operation state.
design.scheduler: Existing RecoveryService sweep; initial 1s, exponential backoff capped at 30s, at most 8 due hints per sweep, terminal/changed/live-owner hints removed. No broad periodic startup scan.
design.commit: Fresh stateQueue ledger/CAS attempt; exact native owner ESRCH plus existing move writer check, path locks held through original proof/fence/terminal atomic persist; scoped thread/interaction/plan/child updates only.
design.sharedLocks: Canonical-dataRoot private file-edit-locks.sqlite serializes short synchronous acquire and dead-PID reclaim metadata transactions, with busy_timeout=0. Own release does not acquire the coordinator: it synchronously verifies regular/non-symlink status, captured dev/ino, native fd identity when present, exact current PID and random token before unlink. No await or background cleanup queue. Foreign updated peers only reclaim proven dead PIDs, so the live releasing owner cannot be replaced; process death prevents late release. Acquisition rollback uses the same ownership-bound helper inside its existing guard.

compatibilityAndLimitations: Valid legacy PID lock records remain supported. Ownerless/malformed legacy records remain busy even when old; age-only reclamation is intentionally removed. A crash before owner record is written remains unknown.
Cross-process exclusion claim is limited to updated cooperating binaries. Older binaries do not obey the new coordinator; mixed-version stale reclamation is not solved.

SQLite coordinator acquisition uses busy_timeout=0; it never waits synchronously for another coordinator transaction. Busy preserves unknown and retries via existing scheduling; I/O/corruption remains a conservative failure.

Per-file owned release remains best effort for arbitrary filesystem/unlink errors; a retained file can remain busy until owner exit. Ordinary coordinator BUSY cannot block own release because release no longer uses that coordinator. No general I/O cleanup guarantee.
No move replay grants, mixed-operation adapters, multi-move path version chains, directory/cross-filesystem/trash/restore reconciliation or periodic retry of arbitrary failed Runs.
Existing run.recovery.auto informational event de-duplication is not claimed across processes; process tests assert unique operation proof/fence/Run terminal/continuation/physical continuation call.
Local Darwin process-fault evidence only; no power-loss, hostile filesystem or Windows acceptance.
